Case study · CAMP / RUN · DEVCON Manila with Avtica and Amihan

At the frontier: the Philippines’ first Hermes Agentic Code Camp and Hackathon

2026 · National beta

Built with

Preparing Filipino builders for what’s next. Built on Nous Research’s open-source Hermes Agent, CAMP / RUN went from first test to a national code camp beta in two weeks, and 30+ young builders shipped connected AI agents in a single night.

Help us bring this agentic training nationwideSponsor the next one
For global partners and funders

Speed, skill, energy, and scale, in one night

What a partner gets with DEVCON: a community that moves fast, builds for real, and reaches every region of the country.

  • 2 weeksSpeed: from first test to the beta of a national code camp
  • 3 layersTechnical depth: MCP server, skill, and desktop plugin, connected
  • 30+Energy: young Filipino builders across 6 teams, 7 submissions
  • 13Scale: DEVCON locations ready to run the same playbook
Partnerships

Built together, from venue to judging

A volunteer community, a tech company, and an AI firm each carried a layer of the night.

  • Avtica

    Hosted the camp at the Avtica Office in Salcedo Towers, and CTO Dexter John Genterone judged the builds.

  • Amihan Global Strategies

    Taught Hermes Agent fundamentals (Vince Miguel Rosit), ran the live technical demo and built the challenge kit (Karen Pearl Pabilando), and judged.

  • DEVCON Manila and DEVCON HQ

    Organized the camp with a 13-role volunteer team. Founder Winston Damarillo gave the keynote, and Executive Director Dom De Leon kicked off Forge63.

  • Government and cloud

    DOST-ASTI’s Elmer Peramo shared Agham na Ramdam, the agency’s AI initiatives, alongside a session on running agents in AgentCore.

The frontier

Why agentic, why now

AI is moving from answering questions to taking action. Hermes Agent, an open-source agent from Nous Research, turns a plain-language request into real changes in real systems, through tools like GitHub, Google Workspace, Vercel, Neon, and Supabase.

CAMP / RUN gave developers hands-on time with that frontier before it becomes the norm: learn it, see it, build it, run it, prove it, then connect to what’s next.

The tool: Hermes Agent by Nous Research. Open source, runs on your own laptop or a small server, works from the CLI, a desktop app, or Telegram, and connects to real systems through MCP.

Technical process

From install to a connected agent in one night

Every developer set up Hermes on their own laptop, then built on a shared sandbox: Suki Mart, a fictional Filipino retail business.

The team wrote its own 18-page Hermes Agent Complete Setup Guide and a nine-step workshop deck, so a first-time builder can go from zero to a fully connected agent in one sitting.

  1. Install the CLIOne command installs uv, Python, and the launcher; verify, set up a model, health-check.
  2. Desktop appA native window on the same backend; settings and secrets kept in separate files.
  3. Telegram gatewayThe same agent from a phone, locked to one allowed user.
  4. Local hostingRuns as a background service, always on.
  5. Pick a VPSEight providers compared, including free tiers.
  6. Deploy to a VPSNon-root user, firewall, true 24/7 uptime.
  7. MCP serversVercel, Neon, and Supabase from the catalog.
  8. GitHub and Google WorkspaceScoped tokens and OAuth; secrets never in config.
  9. Verify the whole setupCLI, Desktop, Telegram, and five MCP servers, checked.

The challenge: build all three layers, connected

  • The hands (MCP server): wrap the Suki Mart sandbox in domain-specific tools.
  • The playbook (skill): teach Hermes a multi-step workflow using those tools.
  • The face (desktop plugin): a pane or command in Hermes Desktop that runs it.

Connected means a GUI action → skill → MCP → real data back in the GUI. Teams picked a track: Business Operations, Customer Experience, or Open Innovation. AI-assisted coding was allowed.

Judging: 100 points

The three layers carry 60 points; relevance and uniqueness carry 25. Ties go to integration, then relevance.
CriterionWhat judges look forPoints
MCP serverTools run correctly on the sandbox and are domain-specific, not a generic passthrough.20
SkillChains MCP tools into a real multi-step workflow that triggers reliably from a natural prompt.20
Desktop pluginWorks inside Hermes Desktop, is usable, and looks native.20
End-to-end integrationGUI action → skill → MCP → real data back in the GUI.10
RelevanceSolves an actual Business Operations or Customer Experience problem.15
UniquenessAn original idea, not a copy of another team or an existing plugin.10
Demo and pitchClear problem → solution → live proof within five minutes.5
Total100
Energy of young Filipino builders

What they shipped in two hours

Seven submissions from six teams, each solving a real Suki Mart problem with Hermes doing the work. Several are still live today.

  • Suki Command CenterTeam Bantay Suki · an MCP server, a skill, and a desktop plugin for store operationsSee it live (opens in a new tab)
  • Suki PromiseGuardTeam GitGitAW · evidence-backed customer recovery operationsSee it live (opens in a new tab)
  • Suki PulseA solo build · turns customer complaints into root causes and operational fixesSee it live (opens in a new tab)
  • Suki Mart storefront agentTeam I love DevCon · a customer-facing store connected to HermesSee it live (opens in a new tab)
  • Three-layer starter buildTeam Nexus · MCP server, skill, and desktop plugin, open on GitHubView the code (opens in a new tab)
  • Live laptop demosTeams Axon Enjin and x44 · served straight from their laptops through secure tunnels during demos
Venue and run of show

One room, one night, every minute planned

The Avtica Office at GF Salcedo Towers hosted the full program from a 10 AM team call to an 11:30 PM egress. Teams were grouped five at a time in arrival order, team API keys were released only on cue, and every demo was timed from the first word.

  1. 10:00 AMTeam call, setup, and final practice
  2. 3:00 PMRegistration and team grouping
  3. 4:00 PMOpening and pre-event survey
  4. 4:10 PMKeynote: Winston Damarillo
  5. 4:20 PMHermes Agent fundamentals
  6. 5:10 PMAgham na Ramdam: AI initiatives by DOST-ASTI
  7. 5:40 PMRunning agents in AgentCore
  8. 6:10 PMHermes Agent technical demo
  9. 7:00 PMBuild challenge briefing and rubric
  10. 7:10 PMTwo-hour team build (the clock runs through dinner)
  11. 9:10 PMBuild freeze and judges
  12. 9:20 PMFive-minute live demos
  13. 10:25 PMForge63 kickoff
  14. 10:45 PMWinners and photos
  15. 11:30 PMEgress
Nationwide scale

From one room to 13 locations

Two weeks after the first internal test, the format ran live as the beta of a national code camp. DEVCON’s chapter network can carry it to every region: 13 locations across Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao, a 60,000+ strong community, and 120+ free events every year, run by local volunteer officers.

  • A playbook, not a one-off: a setup guide, a challenge kit and sandbox, a 100-point rubric, and a named role sheet with handoffs.
  • Low barrier to entry: Hermes runs on the participant’s own laptop, with a free local option and a phone-ready Telegram gateway.
  • Repeatable format: learn, build for two hours, demo in five minutes. The same run of show works in any city.
  • A next step: builders move on to Forge63, so the momentum continues after the night ends.
